content: 1. Carefully measure the prescribed dose of the liquid form of this medication using a special measuring device or spoon to ensure accuracy. Avoid using household spoons, as they may not provide the correct measurement. 2. The dosage and duration of treatment are determined based on your specific medical condition and your response to the therapy. It is essential to follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. 3. Take this medication regularly as prescribed to achieve the maximum therapeutic benefit. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. 4. Do not increase your dose or take this medication more frequently than directed by your healthcare provider. Doing so may increase the risk of side effects without improving your condition. 5. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if you feel better before completing the course. Stopping the medication prematurely may result in a recurrence of symptoms. 6. If you are using nonprescription cimetidine for self-treatment of acid indigestion or heartburn, take one tablet orally with a glass of water as needed. To prevent heartburn, take one tablet orally with a glass of water right before or up to 30 minutes before consuming food or beverages that trigger heartburn. 7. Do not exceed two tablets in a 24-hour period unless specifically instructed by your doctor. 8. Common side effects of this medication may include headache, dizziness, drowsiness, or diarrhea. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. 9. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek immediate medical attention. 10. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance regarding side effects. 11. Before taking cimetidine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other H2 blockers (such as famotidine, nizatidine, or ranitidine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. 12. Some symptoms may indicate a more serious underlying condition. Consult your doctor if you experience persistent or worsening symptoms. 13. Liquid forms of this medication may contain sugar and/or alcohol. Use caution if you have diabetes, liver disease, or any condition requiring you to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. 14. This medication may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. 15. Limit alcoholic beverages while taking this medication. Older adults may be more sensitive to its side effects, particularly confusion and lung infections (such as pneumonia). 16. During pregnancy, cimetidine should only be used when clearly needed. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Cimetidine passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. 17. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, nonprescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 18. Cimetidine can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Additionally, by reducing stomach acid, it may alter the absorption of certain medications, impacting their effectiveness. 19. Examples of drugs that may be affected include atazanavir, dasatinib, certain azole antifungals (such as itraconazole and ketoconazole), levoketoconazole, pazopanib, and sparsentan, among others. Inform your doctor if you are taking any of these medications. 20. Cigarette smoking can interfere with the effectiveness of this medication. Discuss smoking cessation options with your healthcare provider. 21. Cimetidine and similar H2 blockers (such as famotidine, nizatidine, and ranitidine) are available both with and without a prescription. Consult your doctor to determine the most appropriate option for your condition. 22. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 23. Lifestyle changes, such as participating in stress reduction programs, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol intake, and making dietary adjustments (e.g., avoiding caffeine and spicy foods), may enhance the effectiveness of this medication. 24. Your doctor may recommend laboratory and/or medical tests while you are taking this medication to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all scheduled medical and lab appointments. 25. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 26. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. 27. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
